summary: Lower a class declaration to a generated C# type only when the class binding is not observed as a first-class JavaScript value and no TDZ-sensitive access occurs.

target.notes: Emit a generated C# class for the JavaScript class and rewrite statically resolved construction/member operations to that generated type. This rule does not model the JavaScript constructor object itself.

caveats: C# types are not JavaScript constructor objects.
Class declarations are lexical and TDZ-sensitive; native type emission is allowed only when that distinction is unobservable.

tests.name: simple declaration and construction
tests.input: class Point { constructor(x) { this.x = x; } } console.log(new Point(3).x);
tests.expected_csharp: public sealed class Point { public double x; public Point(double x) { this.x = x; } }

tests.name: edge: class used as value requires another rule
tests.expected_behavior: prints function; this rule must not match because the class binding is reflected as a JavaScript value
